# Pitex 1.1.1

The Assistant model menu lists models from every backend you leave on.
Settings turns those backends on and off with switches.

## Changes

- The model menu lists pi, Claude Code, and Apple Foundation Models on a
  Mac that can run them.
- Settings no longer picks one backend. Each backend that Settings shows
  has a switch. The menu lists models only from the backends you leave on.
- If you turn off the backend that is running, Pitex stops that turn and
  continues on the first backend that is still on in the Settings list.
  If you turn off a backend that is not running, Pitex only removes its
  models.
- If you turn every switch off, Pitex stops the running turn. The menu is
  empty. Pitex does not start a session.
- Choosing a model on another backend switches to that backend and starts
  a new session. If the panel already has messages, they stay and Pitex
  adds one notice. Pitex does not replay that chat into the new session.
  Choosing a model on the current backend only changes the model.
- The model menu no longer stays locked after you pick a model.
- Pressing Send, or opening the model menu, no longer crashes the window.

## Install

Pitex 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 update to 1.1.1 from Settings or, with automatic
installation enabled, at launch. For Homebrew installations, run
`brew update` and `brew upgrade --cask pitex`.

Builds from the earlier 2.x line do not update automatically; install 1.1.1
from the downloads below. Pitex Nightly continues to use its separate
update channel.

## Downloads

Downloads include the macOS ARM64 DMG, Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 AMD64 DEBs,
Windows AMD64 installer and portable ZIP, the Ubuntu installer, and
SHA256SUMS.
Windows remains beta.
